0.11.0.text: SFX Kit has its own page, beside Library: listen to every sound by category or search them all, then ask Claude for one by its id. A sound named in a script or storyboard shows as a pink SFX pill: hover over it to listen.
Pages are tighter, with half the space above each section.

0.10.0.text: Richer films: every scene is drawn in a world made for your video, with depth and gentle movement, and moves between your brand's dark, light and accent grounds. Each storyboard scene has a plan under The plan, and the build starts from the frames you approved.

Before Claude reviews a draft, Video Studio's own checks go over it: words too small or gone too soon for a phone, anything outside the safe areas or off your brand, words that land after they're said, and the sound's level and balance. Every draft is scored on its story too: one clear message, a hook that pays off and one clear ask.

Quicker: checks, storyboard frames and library stills draw on the graphics chip, a round of fixes checks only what changed, and on a 3D film both take seconds rather than many minutes. New videos use HyperFrames 0.9.16, with quicker renders and real motion blur.

One review room: the script, storyboard and video pages share one layout, with your notes beside the content. Pages open from a link at the top of Claude's message, and the band above the message box shows only the videos you're working on in that session.

The full library adds Interface and Forms (browser and app windows, devices, messages, social posts, forms and controls), five split screens and captions that move. Brand kits have backgrounds, brand pages show your fonts as they are, and library colours read in every brand.

Video Studio has its own guides now, for every part of a film from motion and design to story, captions, sound and footage. Setup installs no outside skills into your studio, and Studio health offers to remove the ones an older setup put there.

0.9.0.text: Tidy up finished videos: once a video is delivered, Video Studio can remove its drafts, review stills, replaced storyboards and edit history, after you say yes. The delivery page and Studio health show how much space each one would free.
Voiceovers are always your own: a recording, or one read from the approved script by a voice artist or any voice service. The script page's Copy the voiceover button gives you its words.
Video Studio keeps HyperFrames on the version it's tested with, and turns off the anonymous usage data that HyperFrames, the skills tool and Homebrew would otherwise send.

0.8.0.text: Sound effects from SFX Kit: 320 sounds, each placed exactly on its moment and set under the voiceover. Claude adds them while it builds a video, as many as the brief calls for.
A brand kit can have a logo ident: the brand's sound for its logo, which plays on the brand's page.
Setup installs everything Video Studio needs without asking about each part, and an update downloads anything new in the background. Renders use the graphics chip by themselves on Apple silicon.

0.7.1.text: Point at it: on a paused video or a storyboard frame, press Box or Arrow and drag to show exactly what you mean. Claude gets a picture of that moment with your mark on it.
Only the library items you can use can be starred as favourites.

0.7.0.text: Search the library as you type, and star the items you like: Video Studio suggests your favourites first.
Try any library item with your own words on its page, and watch the preview play them.
A delivery page for every finished video: each file to download, captions, and the words to go with it.
Setup and Studio health: a page that shows what's installed, and what to say to Claude to fix anything that isn't.

0.6.3.text: Watch it being made: while Claude works, a video's overview shows the steps, the newest frames and Video Studio's own scores.

0.6.2.text: Hover a library tag in a script or storyboard to see the item playing in your brand.
Review pages are shorter: the notes fold away, and the save button says what saving does.
